Daniel has brought back this proposal for you to evaluate:

Gemini can describe a complex building or generate code for one. Inside X-Ray, it must turn that idea into operations the app exposes. Currently:
- Limited geometry: walls, openings, slabs and roofs cannot efficiently express twisting towers, curved facades, intricate trusses or realistic terrain.
- Too much manual assembly: repeating 2,000 facade panels should be one parameterised operation. Making Gemini specify each piece creates slow, fragile work.
- Weak correction tools: complex modelling needs selecting groups, changing parameters, regenerating connected parts and rolling back failed attempts.
- Limited visual feedback: successful tool execution only means the app accepted the operation. Gemini needs useful views and measurements to discover that the resulting building looks wrong.
- Execution limits: context, tool rounds, output size and rendering performance eventually matter. Raising those limits alone doesn't supply missing modelling capabilities.
Nothing fundamental prevents us from attempting something extremely hard now. But with the current tools, it will spend much of its effort assembling approximations.
The biggest upgrade is a procedural modelling workspace: let Gemini generate and run constrained geometry code in an isolated preview, inspect the result, then save it as editable project geometry with undo. Keep deterministic checks around that execution.
That would support substantially more ambitious creation. Whether a result is structurally sound or follows verified plans remains a separate question from whether Gemini can model it convincingly.
